subcompetencies.name: Patient Evaluation and Clinical Decision Making

level_1: With assistance, integrates information with patient-specific factors to design a succinct diagnostic, work-up, and management plan of a medically uncomplicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
level_2: With assistance, integrates information with patient-specific factors to design a succinct diagnostic, work- up, and management plan of a medically complicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
level_3: Independently integrates information with patient- specific factors to design a succinct diagnostic, work-up, and management plan of a medically uncomplicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
level_4: Independently integrates information with patient-specific factors to design a succinct diagnostic, work-up, and management plan of a medically complicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
level_5: Appraises gaps in literature and proposes research related to diagnostic work-up and multidisciplinary treatment

Independently moves fluidly through the course of rare operations and refines operative plans as needed
level_5: Moves forward in therapeutic or interventional procedures with active direction
Independently chooses and assembles instruments
Anticipates and prevents intra-operative complications for rare procedures

subcompetencies.name: Tissue Handling of Delicate (oncologic, inflamed, and scarred tissue) and Neonatal Tissue

level_1: Demonstrates limited skill in handling delicate and neonatal tissue
Visualizes tissue plane, and identifies and dissects relevant normal anatomy
level_2: Requires prompting to identify appropriate tissue planes
Adapts tissue handling based on tissue quality
level_3: Demonstrates adequate but inconsistent handling of delicate and neonatal tissue
Visualizes tissue planes and identifies and dissects relevant abnormal anatomy
level_4: Identifies appropriate plane but requires redirection to maintain dissection in the optimal tissue plane
Demonstrates efficiency and instructs other learners in techniques to identify and manipulate delicate and neonatal tissue in rare procedures
level_5: Consistently demonstrates careful handling of delicate and neonatal tissue
Develops new instrumentation and techniques for delicate and neonatal tissue

level_1: With assistance, manages the post- operative course of an uncomplicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
Follows an evidence based long-term management plan
level_2: Identifies the rationale for a long-term management
Independently manages the post-operative course of a complicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
level_3: Independently manages the post-operative course of an uncomplicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
Integrates patient- and patient family-specific factors in the construction of an evidence-based long- term management plan
level_4: Describes a general long- term management plan
Identifies gaps in post- operative management, and creates pathways to address these through quality improvement/research initiatives
level_5: With minimal assistance, manages the post- operative course of a complicated neonatal or pediatric surgical patient
Identifies knowledge gaps in long-term management plans, and creates pathways to address these through quality improvement/research initiatives

level_1: With assistance, recognizes a critically ill neonate or child and begins resuscitation
level_2: Independently recognizes a critically ill neonate or child and begins resuscitation and initial management
level_3: With minimal assistance, individualizes ongoing critical care management and assesses the response to therapy
level_4: Independently individualizes ongoing critical care management and assesses the response to therapy
level_5: Implements novel treatments and care pathways for critically ill children

level_1: With active direction, provides non-operative management of severely injured infants and children

level_3: With minimal prompting, provides non-operative management of severely injured infants and children
Independently provides operative management of severely injured infants and children
level_4: With active direction, provides operative management of severely injured infants and children
Implements novel treatments and care pathways for injured children
level_5: Independently provides non-operative management of severely injured infants and children

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of surgically relevant normal anatomy
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of surgically relevant anatomic variations
level_3: With assistance, identifies surgically relevant anatomic variations and alters patient management accordingly
level_4: Independently identifies surgically relevant anatomic variations and alters patient management accordingly
level_5: Leads advanced anatomy discussion at a multidisciplinary conference and/or in operating room

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of developmental biology and normal neonatal physiology
level_2: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of developmental biology and neonatal physiology and relevant clinical implications
level_3: With assistance, applies knowledge of developmental biology and neonatal physiology into medical decision making
level_4: Independently incorporates knowledge of developmental biology and neonatal physiology into medical decision making
level_5: Recommends novel investigations based on knowledge of developmental biology, neonatal physiology, and new and existing therapies

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of development and physiology of children

level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of patients with common pediatric conditions

level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of patients with common pediatric surgical conditions

level_5: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of patients with complex pediatric surgical conditions

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze an institutional quality improvement project
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of and describes institutional quality improvement initiatives
Independently (supervision only) discloses patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
level_3: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional level
level_4: Participates in institutional quality improvement initiatives

level_5: Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination, including transitions of care
Coordinates with local resources to effectively meet the needs of a pediatric surgical patient population
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the pediatric surgical population health needs
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines, including transitions of care
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams, including transitions of care
Participates in changing and adapting individual practice to provide for the needs of specific pediatric surgical populations
level_4: Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local pediatric surgical population
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements, including transitions of care
level_5: Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional teams, including transitions of care
Leads innovations and advocates for pediatric surgical populations with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, pediatric rehabilitation facility, finance, personnel, technology, payment systems)
level_2: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts pediatric surgical patient care
level_3: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_4: Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
level_5: Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transition of care for the pediatric surgical population

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use the available evidence and how to incorporate the patient’s and patient’s family’s preferences and values into the care of patients
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits the patient’s and patient’s family’s preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with the patient’s and patient’s family’s preferences, to the care of patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertain and/or conflicting evidence, to guide care, tailored to the individual patient and the patient’s family
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for patients and patients’ families; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Consistently seeks performance data with adaptability and humility
level_3: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_4: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability and humility
level_5: Seeks performance data episodically with adaptability and humility
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses and how to report them
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles and recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying the care of cancer patients
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_3: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations and takes responsibility for own professionalism lapses
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Takes ownership of system outcomes
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance

level_2: Recognizes limits of the team, with assistance
Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_3: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being

level_4: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being of the team

level_5: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being

level_1: Establishes a professional rapport with patients and patients’ families and communicates in a clear and understandable manner
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability)
Uses shared decision making to align patients’/patients’ families’ values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward patient and patient family encounters and compassionately delivers medical information
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_4: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural differences)
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient and patient family encounters and acknowledges uncertainty in alignment of goals
Role models self- awareness while identifying a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
level_2: Respectfully receives feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care and maintains effective communication in crisis situations
level_3: Communicates information clearly with all health care team members
Communicates feedback and constructive criticism to superiors
level_4: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_5: Uses active listening to adapt communication style to fit team needs
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
Maintains effective and respectful communication during emergent and stressful situations
level_2: Communicates through appropriate channels as required by institutional policy (e.g., patient safety reports, cell phone/pager usage)
Communicates clearly, concisely, timely, and in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Role model for individual communication across the system
level_4: Demonstrates efficient use of appropriate channels to communicate with the health care team
Coaches others to improve written communication
level_5: Concisely integrates all relevant data from outside systems and prior encounters and reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
